findings.text: Under pull_request GitHub runs the workflow and the script from the pull request's own merge commit, so a branch (or an approved fork) that edits from-main.sh or the job's if reports 'Only from main' green.
findings.note: In two steps, because production holds no copy of the workflow yet and pull_request_target runs production's copy: checkpoint 1 bootstraps with pull_request for the one first merge, which comes from main (avenMAIA opens it from main); checkpoint 2 moves 'Only from main' into its own workflow, .github/workflows/theos-from-main.yml, on pull_request_target with no checkout and the test inline, so production's copy decides, removes the job from theos.yml (a skipped job of that name would count as passed), and test.sh asserts both. Written into c1 and checkpoint 2.

findings.text: upload-artifact refuses a name already used in the run, so a re-run of 'theOS' could go red on the upload alone.
The tools are tried on amd64 only; arm64's answer is inherited from the image workflow's smoke by digest.
findings.note: c1 says so: arm64's tools are proven by avensandbox-image.yml's smoke of each platform before the join; box.sh checks the manifest for both and tries the tools on the runner's amd64.

findings.text: d-70 and d-58 do not resolve; they are d-c219 and d-4ca4.
The test does not check the required jobs' if conditions; an added if that skips a ready pull request would pass.
findings.note: test.sh asserts each required job's if is one of the two draft guards; tried: a job changed to run only on push turns the test red.

findings.text: GitHub keeps one waiting run per concurrency group, so a third push to production cancels the second's waiting run.
findings.note: Written in the workflow and in c3: the newest commit holds every earlier change and is the one checked and deployed.

findings.text: Since GitHub's change of 8 Dec 2025, pull_request_target takes its workflow from the default branch (main), not the base branch, so 'production's own copy' never decides.
findings.note: The pull_request_target step is dropped (see the next finding); c1 no longer says it.

findings.text: A required check is matched by name and source only; a pull request can add a workflow with a job named 'Only from main' (or 'avenSANDBOX', 'theOS') that passes, so no workflow-level fix stops someone who can open a pull request with workflows.
findings.note: c1 and the assumptions now say the checks catch mistakes, not someone with write access, and that merging into production takes write access. A guard no pull request can fake is Samuel's choice: the question in aip-59ad's questions (accept, an organization ruleset 'Require workflows to pass', or approval for outside contributors' runs). Not tested on GitHub: the spoof is not tried.
